title: Numerical experiments for Graph-Induced Tensor Liftings for Networked SEIR Models
description: Software and numerical data accompanying Graph-Induced Tensor Liftings for Networked SEIR Models: Dimensional Reduction and Residual Analysis. Includes original SEIR simulations; complete ordered, symmetric and reachable Carleman comparisons; graph-specific residual bounds; source-node sensitivity; sparse operator memory and timing experiments; synthetic large-network tests; and finite-horizon truncation-accuracy diagnostics. An additional structural benchmark uses the public SocioPatterns InVS workplace face-to-face contact dataset (92 participants, 755 observed pairs) and 30 seeded, size- and edge-matched random networks. Recorded contacts are aggregated to a fixed graph support; within-node diagonal channels and weights are modeling assumptions. This is not a calibrated epidemic forecast or a claim of convergence of the truncation hierarchy. All numerical tables (Tables 2–9) and data-derived figures (Figures 2–5) are mapped to reproducible programs, input data and outputs in doc/REPRODUCIBILITY_INDEX.md. Version 1.0.4 extends the scientific baseline v1.0.2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21427810) and succeeds the documentation/metadata release v1.0.3 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22080488).
